documents.title: Labor and delivery discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - LABOR & DELIVERY
Discharge Summary
Admitted 01/01/2025 09:20   Discharged 01/04/2025 11:40
Patient: Grace Paquette   DOB 11/02/1992

Presentation: 32-year-old G3P2002 at 39w0d with contractions every five minutes for the past two hours. About a week ago painful blisters appeared on the vulva. She has known recurrent genital herpes, quiet for more than a year, and took no antiviral prophylaxis in this pregnancy. Pregnancy otherwise routine. Her first birth was vaginal; her second (01/2024) was vaginal with a repaired third-degree laceration.

On arrival: T 37.2 C (99.0 F), BP 120/78. Fetal tracing category I.
Exam: clusters of vesicles and shallow ulcerations over both labia majora. Speculum exam: cervix free of lesions. Lesion swab sent for HSV PCR; HSV-2 detected.

Course: With active genital lesions in labor, cesarean delivery was recommended and she agreed. Primary low transverse cesarean under spinal anesthesia; liveborn infant handed to the newborn team. Uncomplicated surgery and recovery. She restarted her own valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily for 3 days on postoperative day 1 for the outbreak; lesions crusting at discharge.

Discharge diagnoses: term pregnancy delivered by primary low transverse cesarean; active genital HSV at term (HSV-2). History of third-degree laceration, healed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: incision check 2 weeks, postpartum visit 6 weeks.

cc: Primary care

documents.title: Post-delivery call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called to let us know - baby came 1/1 by C-section because she had an outbreak when labor started. Home since Saturday. Finished the 3 days of valacyclovir, sores almost gone. Incision sore, no redness or drainage, no fever. Walking around the house. Hospital will send summary. Postpartum appt with PCP set for Feb.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Postpartum Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
6 wks after primary LTCS 1/1/25 for an HSV outbreak in labor (PCR HSV-2). Saw OB for the incision check; postpartum OB visit next week.

Feels well. Sores healed within about 10 days, nothing since. Incision comfortable. Bowel control normal, no leakage. Mood good, PHQ-9 2. Plans to go back to teaching after February break.

Exam: Well. Low transverse incision healed, no erythema. Abdomen soft. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P
1. HSV outbreak at term - resolved. Back to episodic valacyclovir; she has tablets at home.
2. Hx 3rd-degree laceration 2024 - stable, no symptoms.
3. S/p cesarean - healing well.
Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Valacyclovir refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic request from pharmacy: valacyclovir 500 mg #18. Last filled 10/2022, used in January. Episodic use, on list. Approved per PCP protocol, 1 refill.

documents.title: Pregnant again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - positive test this evening, LMP was 4/3. Not exactly the plan but here we are! Can you put in the OB referral again please?

documents.title: RE: Pregnant again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, Grace. Referral to your OB group is in. Since the C-section was only in January, they'll want to see you soon to talk through the plan. Hold the valacyclovir unless they say otherwise.

documents.title: Obstetrics: new OB visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS GROUP
New OB visit 05/27/2025

G4P3003 at 7w6d by LMP 04/03/2025, ultrasound concordant; EDD 01/08/2026. Single intrauterine pregnancy.

History: vaginal births 2017 and 01/2024 (third-degree laceration, repaired); primary low transverse cesarean 01/2025 for active HSV in labor. Interpregnancy interval about 3 months. Recurrent genital HSV. NKDA.
Prenatal labs drawn, unremarkable.

Delivery options after cesarean to be discussed at the next visit.

Obstetrics attending

documents.title: Obstetrics: delivery planning
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS GROUP
Prenatal visit 07/15/2025, 14w6d

We discussed trial of labor after cesarean versus elective repeat cesarean. One prior low transverse cesarean (operative report reviewed), plus two prior vaginal births. We reviewed the benefits of a successful vaginal birth and the risks of a trial of labor, including uterine rupture. Ms. Paquette chooses a trial of labor after cesarean; she will labor on our unit with continuous fetal monitoring. Consent signed; plan to revisit near term.

Obstetrics attending

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. 32F, G4P3, 24w6d, EDD 1/8/26. OB says all routine. She and OB have settled on a trial of labor after the January cesarean.
No HSV outbreaks since January. Bowels normal.
No alcohol. Mood ok, a lot going on with three kids, PHQ-2 1. School year started.

Exam: Gravid, fundus about umbilicus. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
- Preventive: CBC for OB. Flu and COVID in a couple of weeks at a nurse visit; Tdap with OB in the third trimester. Pap/HPV due next year - after delivery.
- Episodic valacyclovir on hold in pregnancy.
Next physical fall 2026.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count normal for where you are in the pregnancy. Sent to OB.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 27 wks. Well, afebrile. Trivalent flu L arm, 2025-26 Pfizer COVID R arm. 15 min observation, tolerated. Record printed for her OB folder.

documents.title: Leave forms
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The district wants a medical certification from my doctor for maternity leave starting in late December. OB says they only do the delivery part and the district also needs my primary. Do I need to come in for that?

documents.title: RE: Leave forms
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Grace, the doctor would like a quick visit to go over the form. We have Tuesday 12/2 at 3:45. Bring the form with you. You're booked - reply if that time doesn't work.

documents.title: Obstetrics: prenatal update
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS GROUP
Prenatal visit 11/18/2025, 32w5d

Doing well. Growth on track, BP normal. Tdap given. She continues to plan a trial of labor after cesarean; reviewed signs of labor and when to come in. Weekly visits from 36 weeks.

Obstetrics attending

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, straightforward MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with the district leave certification. 34w6d, G4P3, EDD 1/8/26, prenatal care with OB, planning TOLAC.

Feels well. Busy end of semester. No HSV symptoms.

Vitals normal. Comfortable, no edema.

Form completed: pregnancy with expected delivery in early January; leave from 12/22/2025, expected 12 weeks; certifying provider for delivery and recovery details is OB. Copy scanned.

We'll see her after the baby comes. Call with anything.

documents.title: Forms faxed
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Leave certification signed and faxed to the district HR number she gave. Confirmation page scanned. Left her a VM.

documents.title: Labor and delivery / ICU discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - LABOR & DELIVERY
Discharge Summary
Admitted 01/01/2026 01:50   Discharged 01/05/2026 11:30
Patient: Grace Paquette   DOB 11/02/1992

Admission: 33-year-old G4P3003 at 39w0d in spontaneous labor, attempting a trial of labor after one prior low transverse cesarean (01/2025, for active HSV). Other births vaginal (2017; 01/2024 with a repaired third-degree laceration). Recurrent genital HSV, no lesions on admission. Uncomplicated pregnancy. NKDA. Admission hemoglobin 12.1.

Course: Contractions every 2 to 3 minutes. She reached complete dilation and had been at 10 cm with the vertex at +1 station for about an hour when the fetal heart rate fell abruptly from a baseline of 140 to 60 and did not recover for more than 3 minutes. At the same time she reported sudden, sharp lower abdominal pain. The uterus was firm, tense and tender; vaginal bleeding was minimal. Uterine rupture suspected and emergency cesarean called.

Operative findings: rupture through the prior low transverse scar with hemoperitoneum. Liveborn infant delivered and handed to the neonatal team. The uterine defect was repaired in two layers; the uterus was preserved. Estimated blood loss 1,700 mL. Two units of packed red cells transfused.

Postoperative: transferred to the ICU for overnight monitoring after the hemorrhage; hemodynamically stable, hemoglobin 7.8 after surgery. Transferred to postpartum floor 01/02. Ambulating, tolerating diet, incision clean. Hemoglobin 8.6 on 01/05.

Discharge diagnoses: uterine rupture during trial of labor after cesarean; emergency repeat cesarean with repair of uterine rupture; acute blood loss requiring transfusion. Recurrent genital HSV.
Discharge medications: ferrous sulfate 325 mg by mouth once daily for 3 months.
Counseling: any future pregnancy must be delivered by planned cesarean before the onset of labor; she should not labor again. Recommend early prenatal care if she conceives.
Follow-up: incision check 1 to 2 weeks; postpartum visit with CBC at 6 weeks.

cc: Primary care

documents.title: Outside records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hospital summary reviewed: TOLAC 1/1 ended in uterine rupture at the old scar, emergency cesarean and repair, uterus kept, 2 u PRBC, a night in the ICU. Hgb 8.6 at discharge, on iron per OB. OB following postpartum. Filed. Will reach out to her.

documents.title: Checking in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Grace, I read the hospital summary and I'm so sorry it was such a frightening delivery. I hope you and the baby are settling in at home. OB will see you for the incision and your six-week visit and recheck your blood count. Once you're up to it, I'd like to see you here too - no rush, just let the front desk know.

documents.title: RE: Checking in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you, that means a lot. We're home and doing okay - still pretty wiped out and the incision is sore but getting better every day. Taking the iron. I'll call once things calm down.

documents.title: Obstetrics: postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS GROUP
Postpartum visit 02/10/2026

Ms. Paquette is six weeks after emergency cesarean with repair of a uterine rupture. Incision well healed. Lochia resolved. Energy improving. Hemoglobin today 11.0, up from 8.6 at discharge; finish the 3-month iron course.

We again reviewed that any future pregnancy requires a scheduled cesarean before labor begins and early prenatal care.
Mood screen negative. Cleared for usual activity.

Obstetrics attending

documents.title: Outside records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: OB postpartum note: healed, Hgb 11.0. Filed.

documents.title: Valacyclovir refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy e-request: valacyclovir 500 mg tab, 1 BID x3 days at outbreak onset, #18. On active list, episodic. Approved 1 refill per protocol. Pt not seen since 12/2025 - flag to schedule.

documents.title: Physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I know I owe you a visit. Summer is chaos with four kids home. Could I do my physical in the fall? I'll call in August once I know my teaching schedule.

documents.title: RE: Physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Of course - just call or message when you know your schedule and we'll find a morning that works.
